keyFindings.description: The retry ceiling restores the idle ping for one room, not for the listener, and two statements say otherwise. staleRoomRetryBackoff backs one room's window off to a ceiling of 2 * DefaultListenIdle, and the constant's comment concludes that past the idle period the wake is the listener's again, so it waits its idle period out and pings. But wakeIn returns the minimum over every deferred room, and waitFor takes the evictor's wake whenever it is under the idle period, so the ceiling bounds a room's window and not the thing waitFor compares. Three rooms in simultaneous runs of no-verdict re-examinations, entering more than a few seconds apart, settle at their own phase plus the ceiling, so the gaps between consecutive wakes are the arrival offsets modulo the ceiling: three rooms 20 s apart give gaps of 20, 20, 20, every one under DefaultListenIdle, and listen takes the waking branch on every round and never reaches the ping. It is a stable fixed point rather than a transient, since no ping means no idle wait to bunch the rooms back together, which is what rescues the two-room case. Simulated against the exact functions over 6,000 s of steady state: one room 199 pings, two rooms 100, three rooms at 20 s offsets 0, three at 25 s offsets 0, four at 15 s offsets 0. One and two rooms are safe structurally, since the gaps sum to the ceiling. Harm needs the LISTEN socket to go half-open as well - the ping is the only detector this file names, since WaitForNotification on such a socket returns deadline-exceeded rather than an error and pgx keeps the connection open - and whether the dialer's TCP keep-alive would eventually error it is unverified from this workspace (the module cache holds no pgx source), so it is not counted as a mitigation. The round's own in-flight-write arm widens the set of rooms that can sit in permanent no-verdict runs, so the two halves of this round interact. Part of this is mine: in round 5 I offered the evictor-side ceiling and the listener-side fix and said either answers it, which was wrong. The fix to take is the listener-side one, which the body itself named and set aside: in listen, track the last proven round trip - the dial's LISTEN, a received notification, a successful ping - and ping when that is older than idle() whatever ended the wait. About ten lines in one function; the other two callers set neither hook, so with no wakes the proven stamp is the last ping and their behaviour is byte-for-byte what it is today. It also puts the invariant in the package that owns the connection, where a second NextWake caller cannot silently re-open it with one room each. Keeping the evictor-side ceiling alone is acceptable only if both statements come down to their real scope and the limit goes in the risk list. Both thermonuclear passes found this independently, from different directions.

The enumeration rewritten this round says every return from documentChanged is either a verdict or an attempt that got no answer, and the first return in the body is neither: the interval refusal defers the room on its own window and touches neither reachedVerdict nor armRetry. The code is right - an interval refusal must not count as a failed attempt, or a burst would inflate the backoff - but the sentence is one clause short, and it is the same shape of defect round 4 blocked on.

The multiprocess build tag and its CI job are in no document, where the repository's own convention documents exactly this for the memory tag beside it (cmd/dispatch/AGENTS.md gives the tag, why it is tagged, its CI job name and the command). A developer running the documented checks never runs the two-process suite, and this pull request's evidence rests on it. Also carried as hardening: leasePoolSize's zero headroom makes the next leased loop a ninth caller that waits for the length of the longest pass with nothing failing or logging, and a Listener with Channels set and OnNotify nil now drops every notification silently where it used to panic - the right call at that layer, but findable only by its silence.

roundFiveFindingsAnswered: the in-flight-write return: fixed in 006069a2 with armRetry, the enumeration corrected to call it an attempt, and reachedVerdict added on all four verdict returns with the fifth clearing through recordEviction. Verified at the head: attempts cannot leak (its keys stay a subset of deferred), cannot carry a stale count across an interval refusal (a room holding a count cannot have been evicted inside the interval), and the retry against a long-running writer costs two map lookups and no round trip, since the guard sits ahead of the head read
the unbounded re-arm: answered on the evictor's side with a per-room backoff to a ceiling of 2 * DefaultListenIdle, which is sound for one and two rooms and is the important finding above for three

the minors: events.Stream.CloseAll's Test-only note replaced with its production caller, the two clock-origin facts in the test comments corrected (the gap under-reads and the guard is permissive; the 4 s budget's origin is the helper's own timer, about 4.1 s from the trailing write), pglisten now nil-checks OnNotify, and the census lead-in rewritten to describe the call-graph enumeration and its four surfaces. Register's trap and Evict's unbounded context are stated as residuals rather than fixed, which is what I asked for
